text: Task commit subjects must place the em-dash DIRECTLY after the phase number: gate.mjs phaseOwnFiles greps the literal 'phase <N> —', so 'feat(scope): phase 1 task 1.1 — ...' matches NOTHING and every file in that commit is classified foreignCommitsInRange. The gate then derives testScope/reviewScope/specialist floors from an almost-empty phase-own set. Correct form: 'feat(scope): phase 1 — task 1.1: <what>'. Unrecoverable once sibling sessions have interleaved commits into the range, because the fix would be a rebase over their work.

The arc prompt classified 'measure --flow do-arc --assert 12500' as one of three ENVIRONMENTAL host failures. It is not: it is a repo-state standing red measuring 14917 tokens on any host, already dispositioned in plugins/zeroh-roadmap/DIET-LEDGER.md and assigned to the diet lane, and the gate has no known-failure mechanism to pass over it (green is arithmetic over slot exit codes; checkPhaseConsistency refuses a non-green done flip; PassingGateResultShape refuses passed!==total). The other two WERE real and were fixed in-seam: node_modules/.bin/tsx has a '#!/usr/bin/env node' shebang, so under a PATH-scrubbed test the exec SUCCEEDS and env exits 127 with "env: 'node': No such file or directory" — matching neither the ENOENT branch nor the 'not found' wording, so a fail-OPEN tsx-absent contract was classified as a blocking eval-error. Precedent for the ratchet is phase 1995: escalate, then a user ruling.

When a phase's notes leave a blast-radius ambiguity (widen the SHARED shape or only one use site?), read the step's own verify clause before escalating: a whole-file negative grep can only pass under one of the readings, so the planner already decided it mechanically. Phase 2 task 2.4's `! grep -qF "z.enum(['session', 'codex'])"` spans the file, which is only satisfiable by widening the shared DriverShape — the coherent choice anyway, since a record shape refusing an unknown lane would drop exactly the third-driver phases the arc exists to measure.

A gate slot that exceeds the harness's foreground command cap is not a reason to park or checkpoint: launch the gate run itself with run_in_background so the harness wakes you on exit, and spend the wait on the review round against the already-frozen diff. The plugin's own unit slot (node --test, concurrency 1, ~60 files) runs ~15-20 min against a 10-min Bash cap; splitting it by hand would improvise a scoping command the gate protocol forbids.

A guard's reach rule must be derived from the registry's own declared capabilities, not from what the fixture assumed: the phase-4 parity fixture encoded 'a claude driver cannot reach the codex model', which was false — codex exec is a headless child the plugin's own run lane already uses. The fix was to probe and DECLARE the capability, then re-pin the guard, never to keep the convenient assumption.

A delegated test-writer will hardcode values that a repo-wide ratchet owns (a model id, a path, an argv literal) because its brief names the behaviour, not the ratchets. Phase 9 task 9.4: test-engineer wrote 'gpt-5.6-sol' five times into a fixture and tripped drivers.test.mjs's one-home-for-model-ids scan — invisible to the task's own scoped suite, caught only by a mid-phase FULL run. Two takeaways: name the live ratchets in the delegation brief, and run one full suite mid-phase rather than saving it all for the gate.

A fix round is where the second bug lives: rounds 1, 2 and 3 each found real defects in the PREVIOUS round's fixes — twice a fix had recreated the exact symptom it closed (an archive gate that skipped the already-gone lane; a guard added to one of two, then two of three, call sites). When a review round is a fix round, point the next reviewer AT THE FIX COMMIT and name what each fix was supposed to close, not just at the phase diff.

Before claiming a helper is a shared rail, grep for EVERY call site — twice in phase 6 a guard was added where the reviewer had pointed and missed a third caller (disposeWorktree had three: phase land, arc land, and archiveReviewLane, the last firing from a READ command). Count the call sites first, then fix all of them in one edit.

A gate agent (quality-pass) committed its own fixes with subject 'fix(phase-10): …' — the curate foreign-detector requires the binding 'phase N —' grammar and refused the whole squash range as foreign. Either pass the commit grammar into gate-agent prompts or have the orchestrator own the commit.

fixture-consumer harness runCli dropped ALL stderr on exit-0 runs: execFileSync exposes stderr only on the thrown error object, so success-path advisory lines were silently unobservable and any doesNotMatch(stderr) assertion passed vacuously. Swapped to spawnSync (captures both streams always). Check this when a wired test asserts stderr on a passing command.
PhaseTaskShape requires done:false on every authored task (no schema default) — forgotten on three consecutive plan-phase authorings (10, 11, 13); write it into the task template at authoring time.

A guard-mutation drive done with a string replace can silently hit the WRONG occurrence: mutating "lane === 'plan' && state === 'complete'" in codex.mjs patched nextStepHint (line 751) instead of the statusCodex re-entry key (line 853), and the mutated run came back GREEN — indistinguishable from a vacuous test. A green mutation drive is a claim about the MUTATION as much as about the test: assert the anchor is unique (or patch by line and echo the mutated line back) before believing the result.

A fixture test that drives an admission-gated verb inherits the box's AMBIENT capacity: `arc next` returns action 'blocked' exit 2 once executors busy >= maxExecutors, so test/fixture-consumer/arc-next.test.mjs N1/N4 red on a busy host with nothing wrong in the diff (reproduced at 5 busy vs limit 3 while four sibling codex lanes ran; the same fixture passes by hand at 2 busy). PROVEN remedy, and the trap inside it: pinning ZEROH_ROADMAP_CAPACITY_PROBES alone does NOTHING under a gate slot, because capbuild runs a sanitized systemd unit that STRIPS the variable — the pin only lands with CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV="ZEROH_ROADMAP_CAPACITY_PROBES" (26/26 green pinned, 24/26 unpinned, same tree). Two rules: a gate slot's green silently encodes who else was running, so re-run a RED unit slot serially before reading it as a defect; and an env-seam pin that must survive capbuild has to be declared in CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV or it is a no-op that looks like a refuted hypothesis.

When inserting a new refusal before a named choke point, preserve earlier diagnostic precedence: phase 15.4 required validation before harvest, not before the one-file invariant; the broader placement broke the empty-diff recovery contract.

integrationRefOf reads mergePolicy.autonomousPushRefs[0] (cli/lib/config.mjs), so the LAND TARGET and PUSH AUTHORIZATION are the same field: a consumer that wants `phase land` to work at all must name its integration branch there, and naming it silently authorizes autonomous push to it. There is no way to say 'land here, push nowhere' short of leaving the field unset and losing landing entirely (the fallback is a literal 'develop'). Split the two: an explicit integrationRef key for the target, autonomousPushRefs for the authorization. Surfaced when declaring the ref to unblock landing also enabled a push to a real GitHub origin — and the operator had concluded no origin existed from a `git remote -v | head -2` that truncated it away, which is its own lesson: never conclude absence from a truncated listing.

When extending an ordered operation log, preserve existing first-match semantics: perform prerequisite work before the protected act, but emit the new evidence record after the established outcome record when consumers locate the first entry by target identity.

A CLI test helper built around execFileSync can capture stdout while silently discarding stderr on success; tests for successful stderr signals need spawnSync or an explicit stderr pipe result, plus a failing precondition that proves the signal should exist.

Resolving a rebase conflict BY SIDE ('take landed'/'take lane') silently corrupts two classes a meaning-level merge would not: a GENERATED artifact reverts to its stale form (roadmap.config.schema.json drifted red on the integration branch itself — no phase gate could see it, since every lane gated green pre-land), and a NEW import vanishes while its call site survives (gate.test.mjs lost annotateScopedProbeWarnings and the test died on ReferenceError instead of pinning the behavior). Both escaped review and surfaced only in a later phase's gate. Rules: resolve conflicts by MEANING, re-run generators after any resolution touching a generated file, and re-verify the touched files' implementation SYMBOLS (not the plan's prose) before calling a rebase done — grepping plan wording is not a check on the code.

When a new audit check applies globally, update the shared clean fixture to carry the new valid invariant while keeping violation fixtures explicitly unreviewed; otherwise unrelated tests fail for the new rule instead of their own contract.
When multiple transparencyReport blocks have identical limitations lines, patch with task-specific context; a generic first-match edit can attribute a limitation to the wrong task.

A literal NUL byte written into a .mjs source (here a `${dir}\0${env}` memo key) makes the file BINARY to grep — /bin/grep prints 'binary file matches' and every grep-based repo guard, ratchet and scan over that file silently stops reading its lines. `file <path>` reports 'data' instead of 'JavaScript source'. Use a printable separator (JSON.stringify([a,b])) for composite cache keys in a repo whose guards are greps.

A blind string replace in a multi-step refactor SILENTLY no-ops when an earlier step already changed the anchor: phase 23.4's init.mjs --root plumbing never landed because 23.2 had rewritten the very line it anchored on, and the smoke run only said 'root: roadmap' with no error anywhere. Every scripted edit needs assert old in s (or an equivalent count check) — a replace that matched nothing must be as loud as one that matched wrongly.

roadmap codex run <N> must be launched from the PRIMARY checkout, never from inside a lane worktree: the CLI derives its root from cwd, so a relaunch issued after cd-ing into the lane resolves the journal under the lane, tries to create a nested <lane>-codex-<N> worktree on the already-existing codex/<N> branch, and fails with 'a branch named codex/N already exists' (twice on 2026-09-02/03 for lane 26). Chain 'cd /home/patrik/<repo> &&' explicitly before any codex run, or use git -C for the worktree reads.
Adherence checks over filtered done tasks must compare the filtered count with all planned tasks; Array.every on an empty filtered set creates a false green.
A plugin-local test dependency symlink used for scoped verification must remain through the full gate; removing it before gate run turns unrelated suites red during module collection.

pgrep -f <name> self-matches the probing shell's own argv: a plan verify written literally as bash -c "! pgrep -f graft >/dev/null" can NEVER pass when typed inline, because the Claude/bash wrapper command line contains the pattern. Run residency probes from a script file whose own path and argv do not contain the pattern.

bin/validate-roadmap-file.mjs is a PostToolUse HOOK adapter: it reads its payload from STDIN and ignores argv entirely, exiting 0 on empty stdin. Invoking it as 'node bin/validate-roadmap-file.mjs <file>' therefore validates NOTHING (silent pass) or hangs forever when stdin is an open pipe. The real door for a human or an executor is 'roadmap phase validate <N|path>'.
The adherence negative fixture mutated its in-memory task after the phase file was written, so the scorer still read the original proof; fixture omissions must be applied before serialization.
A combined commit-and-record command cannot know the resulting commit SHA in advance; gate rounds must be recorded only after reading the completed commit hash, never with a placeholder.
A headless `claude -p` arm launched for a phase is killed by the 600s background-wait ceiling mid-phase; launch with CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 (and setsid nohup) from the session shell.

Never spawn a codex child (or a headless claude arm that spawns one) from inside a codex lane's sandbox: the nested child hangs silently. Run opus/headless arms from the session shell, codex lanes from the primary checkout.
Exact substring acceptance checks make prose line wrapping semantically significant; run the literal checks before task state and keep required clauses contiguous.

Native proposal ran roadmap init --help and created then removed scaffold files before approval. Command help must be handled before importing mutating commands; collect filesystem events as well as endpoint hashes so reverted writes remain failures. Dispatcher regression: 10 RED before fix, all 24 init tests GREEN after fix.

Native fixture validation must select the README comparator from the owned fixture shape: Nx uses the immutable emitted catalog; an empty library binds prospective project-root identity. A universal project-root command incorrectly rejects valid workspace rows. Preserve the failed native proposal and rerun after source-bound repairs.

Parse explicit JSON fences with a fence-aware reader. An optional-language regex can mistake a closing shell fence for a new opener and consume the following JSON proposal. Calibrate parsing against full real native responses and keep shell examples and nested fences as negative controls.

Native proof must bind approved gate values and the complete executable command plan to native tool calls; config-to-execution checks alone can certify unapproved drift. Review the evidence contract before freezing costly native runs.
A capbuild systemd service stopped externally can return exit zero before node:test finishes; require terminal TAP totals and schema completion in addition to gate GREEN.

Native read-only behavior evidence needs independently attributable command output and one JSON object per explicit json fence; combined shell output and untagged mixed JSON were retained as rejected captures then refined in the same session.

A delivery fan-in before build is test verification, not an authoritative release manifest; generic promotion hooks also cannot prove no-rebuild. Bind runtime contracts and preserve raw reports, then use fixed provider commands with checksum/version readback.

Release source must be integrated and versioned before native source-bound proof; package or driver changes otherwise invalidate every arm. Preserve incomplete state and historical evidence, review the final source first, then validate once.

Changed-baseline approval must be tested through actual preparation and fan-in; manually constructing an old-baseline plan missed preparation overwriting the prior value. Bind prior Git configuration separately from requested floors.

codex review/plan lanes REUSE an existing worktree at its old HEAD (cli/commands/codex.mjs launch: existsSync(worktree) → return 0) — a re-review after plan repairs graded the UNREPAIRED file. Before relaunching a lane on the same number, reset its worktree to the base (git reset --hard <base>) or dispose it; plugin follow-up: the launcher must reset-or-refuse an existing worktree.

Plan-arc Step 3 Lane B (codex review lanes) looped 4-5 rounds per phase on prose-skill plans: each round found new 'a verify passes an incomplete world' cases because criteria named tokens the step verifies did not assert. Two fixes to plan for: (a) authoring rule — every token a criterion names must be asserted by a step verify (a lint could check criterion tokens against verify commands); (b) plan reviews need the same round cap / delta-only brief as gate rounds (phase 25 covers gates only).

Native fixture writer guards must derive every generated byte from the actual generator and target path: valid underscores are not normalized, and roadmap init schema-relative paths change the config hash when scratch depth changes. Check all before-hashes before the first replacement; retain failed trees and obtain a fresh observed proposal instead of changing an approved writer after mutation.

NATIVEGREEN real startup: arc-plane requested gate plan before the first phase-start commit, then parsed empty output as JSON. Applying the normal do-phase prerequisites and start commit allowed inline-supervised handoff. Phase37 lifecycle wiring must handle this ordering and nonzero CLI output explicitly.

NATIVEGREEN task36.1 governance preflight exposed legacy valid-launch fixtures without runner config. Keep fail-closed production behavior; seed config and phase scope in positive fixtures, and test child-worktree boundaries before install or carry-in. Resume must not reinstall dependencies.

Task36.2 external Claude architect call was rejected before execution: automatic review disallowed sending repository architecture/security details to that destination without specific authorization. No retry or indirect Claude execution. Role resolver selected documented native Sol architect fallback at unreduced rigor; record the substitution, never claim Fable reviewed.

Task36.2 production launcher mutation was rejected by automatic approval review; no source edit was applied or rerouted. Explicit approval is required for persistent sandbox/approval changes and conditional unsafe posture. Review-only proposal is arc-evals/NATIVEGREEN-36.2-approval.md. Approval-never mapping was corrected before asking because protected Git metadata would block required commits; use native approval mediation, with runtime enforcement unverified.

Task 36.2 combined gate exposed cross-field schema gaps after focused launcher checks passed. Inspect raw failing assertions: gate diagnose mislabeled four schema failures authority-quota by matching unrelated successful test output; no new approval was needed.

Task 36.3 official Codex validator rejected the historical hooks:{} sentinel, missing interface, and invalid full-code-review YAML. Architect PROCEED_WITH_FIX: generated schema-native manifest plus explicitly relocated Claude hook config preserves structural host isolation. Disposable official Claude plugin validate accepted ./hooks/claude-hooks.json; raw local evidence .building/nativegreen-36-3-claude-hooks-probe.json. No native runtime activation claim follows from packaging validation.

Task36.4 repeat-test review found invented inventory steps, hook file paths substituted for native event names, and nonexistent fake cache paths. Repair tests to actual prompt-input/details commands and physically installed fixture bytes before implementation; source hashes alone cannot prove installed package bytes.

Pure reducer schemas must parse real accepted and rejected receipts. Invalid input needs a typed raw-evidence rejection branch; rejection must preserve the original authority and safe halt remedy. A negative fixture must actually change its prior state, and schema validation must not normalize stable identity bytes.

When the direct apply_patch tool fails through the broken bwrap sandbox, the local apply_patch executable invoked inside an already-approved escalated exec_command works. Verified in owned /tmp scratch with literal regex backslashes preserved. Prefer that exact patch path over Python string rewrites that can lose quotes or escapes.

Correction freshness must tolerate committing its own review evidence. Use the existing correction checkpoint and recorder-computed bindings; never a global current-HEAD equality rule or model-predicted hashes.

When tightening lane identity, run representative existing launch, archive and harvest fixtures alongside the new tests early. A green new-case matrix alone missed legacy-read crashes and the fact that harvesting advances the requested ref; historical cleanup must remain separate from fresh result reuse.

Convergence coverage must actually re-review the same phase after consuming the previous review and advancing the repair commit. Recording a clean round at a new SHA without a fresh lane run missed an archived-journal restart refusal even though all command-level tests passed. Preserve historical evidence while testing the real repeat-review path.

When adding worktree checks, reuse listWorktrees rather than parsing Git porcelain at a caller. Include older resume fixture homes when strengthening terminal completion bindings; a minimal shipped-summary fixture is no longer a completed-arc fixture once evaluation binding is required.

An adapter must snapshot caller lifecycle state before awaiting native work; cloning it afterward can bind an observation to concurrently changed authority or state. Resume capability absence is a typed hold and never authorizes a fallback start.

Native ownership must verify the canonical stored receipt unconditionally; missing paths, symlinked ancestors and malformed legacy arms cannot bypass verification. Fresh requests bind actual checkout commits before publication, and JSON-unsafe operation values refuse before their meaning can change on disk.

Native process completion is not intent completion. Exercise concrete adapters against real receipt and ownership stores, preserve exact-session resume authority, and atomically persist transport exit with its reducer observation to avoid duplicate native work after a partial write.
Automatic path rewriting must preserve negative test oracles; verify real moved imports through the existing typed schema and run declared consumer tests through the configured runner.

A linked fixture can inherit a legacy config override and an empty registry stub: remove the override and use real discovery before claiming migrated audit coverage; changing unused criterion text does not prove historical intent preservation.

After consolidating a script onto the shared root resolver, assert its typed ambiguity and no-write behavior rather than obsolete private error wording. The gate caught that stale expectation; the corrected test also verifies unchanged phase bytes. Historical migration plans must validate their original Git and stored bytes, not be regenerated with the current rewrite algorithm.

After a consumer-root move, a legacy-layout fixture may remain legacy while its source schema link must resolve the actual checkout. Four arc/derive/gate fixture sources still named the retired schema. Use consumerSchemaPath with the repository root, not a nested plugin directory; focused6 arc and29 derive/resume checks passed after correcting that argument.

A tree-identical curation can remove a completed migration source commit from ordinary ancestry. Reuse existing curate-rescue full-tree bridges, including successive rewrites, rather than invalidate historical completion or add another store. Independent RED preceded repair;55/55 affected checks plus a strengthened wrong-tree control and independent clean review passed. Curation must omit unknown model attribution instead of assuming Claude.

Normalization fixtures must be valid done phases through the real schema and registry, with phase.gateRounds separate from executionResult.gateRounds. Keep the integration branch at base and build on an arc branch. Refusal cases must isolate their target: a canonical phase prefix already proves ownership, so a malformed legacy suffix test must omit that prefix. Exact unknown task notation still refuses before gate freshness.

A crash hook after one prepared commit exposes an intermediate SHA, not the final arc tip. Compare the resumed matching outcome, and bind apply fixtures to a fresh delivery observation so a missing observation cannot masquerade as the intended safety refusal.

Publication authority is exact-head authority: a normalization receipt cannot cover an unpublished descendant, and a red-CI observation taken before local CAS must be refreshed after CAS before a leased provider replacement. Keep local repair HEAD distinct from the published PR/checks HEAD in fixtures and production.

A mutation is evidence only after the same isolated oracle is green without it. The conformance fixture callback edit initially omitted a closing brace; pristine baseline caught syntax failure, no mutation was credited, and syntax was repaired before rerunning the isolated guard checks.

An ownership-bearing registry cannot inherit stale-age lock deletion or accept a missing journal identity as legacy when an incumbent identity exists. Use a kernel-held writer lock and rejoin records at the native launch boundary.

Crash recovery needs the actual bounded operation persisted with its authorization, not only a digest of a caller-owned plan. Cleanup now retains one per-identity operation in the existing registry and distinguishes transient refusal from a durable receipt.

Making cleanup conservative changes normal review reuse: a completed lane may remain present. Preserve its prior journal, prompt and report before resetting for a changed request; test retained and absent worktrees separately, and snapshot file presence independently from directory presence.
Check the full canonical validation boundary before reporting a missing guard in a lower helper; schema parsing may already reject the candidate before that helper runs.
A nonzero ancestry probe is not evidence of divergence: only Git exit 1 means not-ancestor; other failures leave rewrite authority unobserved.
Zod custom refinements are not automatically expressed in generated JSON Schema. Use representable constraints and metadata, then test semantic schema parity as well as generated byte equality.
